title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled, or fried with cheese and meat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑made blend that allows you to make an omelet, scrambled eggs or fried dish without using real eggs. The formula typically contains plant proteins, starch, flavorings and sometimes additives that mimic the taste and texture of eggs. Cheese and meat can be added for a hearty, protein‑rich meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg substitute is a staple in vegan cooking because it is completely plant‑based.
Many blends include nutritional yeast, which gives a characteristic "egg‑like" aroma.
Some brands fortify the product with vitamins B12 and D, nutrients usually found in eggs.
When cooked correctly, the substitute achieves the same fluffiness as a traditional omelet.
It is shelf‑stable and usually sold dry, so no refrigeration is needed before opening.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Unlike real eggs, the substitute contains no cholesterol, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: The blend provides a complete amino‑acid profile to support muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortified versions supply B12, B2 and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Starch and added fiber help maintain regular bowel function.

items.title: Culinary versatility
items.content: Easily combined with cheese, meat, or vegetables for a wide range of flavors.

items.title: Soy or pea protein allergy
items.content: Many substitutes are based on soy or pea protein, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared mixes often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Missing micronutrients
items.content: Compared with eggs, the substitute may lack lutein and choline in sufficient amounts.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: Some brands use artificial flavors and preservatives.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Combine the dry mix with water (or plant milk) in the recommended ratio, whisk to a smooth batter and cook in a lightly oiled pan like a regular omelet. Add grated cheese and diced meat a few minutes before the dish is done so they melt and heat through.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry egg substitute in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. After opening, use within 6–12 months. Cooked batter should be kept refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours.
